findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:

- the shelves underneath the grill tops were heavily accumulated with spilled oils and food debris
- spaces in between standing coolers/freezers and other kitchen equipment were observed with dried grease debris
- the vent covers above the back prep station (near walk in cooler) were observed coated with dried debris.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Crepes were observed with surface temperature of 55F-58F and internal temperature of 85F in the bottom of the cook line prep cooler. Cook stated crepes were made at 6am, and it was a little after 9am when temperature was checked. GM stated the cook starts at 6am, but crepes were likely made around 7am. Process for cooling allows for 30 minute rest period at room temperature prior to placing product in a cooler for chilling. A couple dozen plus crepes were stacked together, which could have also impacted the rate at which product was cooling. GM was advised the prep cooler is not ideal for cooling cooked TCS foods, especially the prep cooler at the west end of the cook line that is in constant use with cooks getting in and out of the cooler throughout operations. Crepes were discarded during inspection. Ensure proper cooling and consider quick chilling smaller stacks or single layers of crepes in the walk-in cooler prior to placing product in the prep cooler. Time stamps are encouraged for working supplies of product that was just prepared and is still in the process of cooling.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Frozen vacuum packaged fish were thawing in the walk-in cooler. Proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish was discussed during the previous routine inspection. GM was advised to work on this practice with staff to ensure proper thawing. Labeling on package states to remove from vacuum pack and thaw under refrigeration temperature. At minimum the packaging needs to be cut open when fish is removed from the freezer to begin thawing in walk-in cooler. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Facility was not in compliance with food handler law. Food handler certification was not available for one of the cooks that has worked at the facility for at least a month. GM is in the process of having staff complete certifications. Ensure copies of food handler certifications are available for all staff without manager certifications at the next routine inspection.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Cod

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Certified food managers have not completed food allergen certification. Requirements for allergen training were discussed at the previous routine inspection, and an informational handout was provided at that time. GM stated CFMs are working on completing food allergen certifications for both locations. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Sever was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handle of manual faucet was touched after handwashing was completed to shut off faucet prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
